sections.h2: Where is South Salt Lake, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
South Salt Lake is a compact city of about 6.9 square miles directly south of Salt Lake City, inside Salt Lake County. Wikipedia describes its boundaries as the Jordan River on the west, 500 East and 700 East on the east, 2100 South on the north and 3900 South on the south.

The 2020 Census counted 26,777 people in 10,448 households, with a median age of 32.0. That is a dense footprint, with roughly 3,857 people per square mile in 2020.

The city is its own municipality, so building permits, code enforcement and business licenses all go through South Salt Lake City Hall at 220 East Morris Avenue.

sections.h2: What is the history of South Salt Lake in brief?
sections.html:
The area was settled in 1847 and later developed around 1890 by Jesse Fox Jr. as Central Park. A Central Park LDS ward formed in 1925, and in 1936 an attempt by Salt Lake City to annex the area failed.

The path to cityhood was bumpy. Residents created the Town of Central Park in August 1936, voters disincorporated it in 1937, and in 1938 they narrowly approved incorporation as South Salt Lake. The town was formally incorporated on September 29, 1938, and became a third-class city on August 1, 1950.

Wikipedia also notes that the world's first KFC franchise opened in the city in 1952, and that the Columbus Center, an early 1900s school building, now holds a county library branch and a senior center.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about South Salt Lake housing?
sections.html:
South Salt Lake is a renter-majority city with small households. The table shows Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 except where marked.

Only about 38 of every 100 occupied homes are owner-occupied. That means a good share of the people who sell here are landlords, so the rental license and tenant questions below come up often.

sections.h2: How do I get around, and what does that mean for buyers?
sections.html:
Transit and freeways are the city's main selling points. The Spaghetti Bowl, where I-15, I-80 and SR-201 meet, sits at the northwest corner, and I-15 and I-80 each have local interchanges.

  • TRAX light rail runs along roughly 200 West with three stations in the city. Blue, Red and Green lines meet at Central Pointe station.
  • The S Line streetcar opened in December 2013 and stops at Central Pointe, South Main, 300 East and 500 East.
  • Census data puts the average commute at about 20 minutes.

Ask a buyer or agent to measure how far your address is from a stop, since walking distance is one of the first things people ask about.

sections.h2: Which schools and public buildings serve South Salt Lake?
sections.html:
Granite School District serves the city. Public elementary schools listed on Wikipedia include Lincoln, Woodrow Wilson and Roosevelt, and Granite Park Junior High covers the middle grades.

Charter options include Alianza (K to 8) and Utah International Charter School (grades 7 to 12). Broadview University has a campus beside city offices, and Utah State University runs a satellite site on State Street.

The school boundaries follow Granite School District maps, so check the address if a buyer asks which school their child would attend.

sections.h2: What does South Salt Lake code enforcement look at?
sections.html:
The city enforces yard, vehicle and property maintenance rules, and it usually starts with a courtesy notice. The code enforcement page says over 90% of issues are settled through communication and education, and unresolved cases can lead to fines and civil prosecution.

  • Lawns and ground cover must stay under 6 inches, and owners must control noxious weeds.
  • Vehicles must be parked on paved surfaces, not grass, dirt or gravel.
  • Inoperable or unregistered vehicles left 30 consecutive days count as a public nuisance.
  • Trash bins go out by 7:00 a.m. on collection day and come back in afterward.
  • Sidewalks must be cleared of snow within 24 hours, leaving a path at least 42 inches wide.

If you inherited a neglected house, an open violation can sit on the property. Clearing it before you sell removes one thing a buyer has to ask about. Call 801-464-6757 to check a property.

sections.h2: What rules apply to rental houses and short-term rentals in South Salt Lake?
sections.html:
Landlords need a city license, and inspections come first. The rental license application states that on-site inspections by the Building Department and Fire Marshal are required before a license is granted, and operating without an approved license is a Class C misdemeanor.

Landlords who complete the Good Landlord Program, which includes training every three years, written leases and background checks on adult occupants, receive a significant reduction in license fees. The city's business license page adds that licenses are not transferable, so a buyer of a rental has to apply on their own.

For short-term stays, the city's STR page says a pending ordinance issued October 15, 2026 stays in place for 180 days or until a new code is adopted. It defines an STR as a stay under 30 consecutive days, requires an owner-occupied duplex, owner-occupied rental or a property owned by a primary resident, and bars STRs in accessory dwelling units.

sections.h2: How are South Salt Lake property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County bills the tax, and payment is due by November 30. The county Treasurer's calendar says December 1 is when unpaid current-year real property taxes become delinquent, and the penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel, reduced to 1% if paid by January 31.

Valuation notices are mailed by July 22, and the Board of Equalization appeal window closes September 15 or 45 days after the notice, whichever is later. A primary residence receives a 45% exemption, so taxable value is 55% of market value. A rental or second home does not receive that exemption.

The Treasurer is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, and the Recorder, who files the deed, is in Suite N1-600 of the same building.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in South Salt Lake?
sections.html:
A cash buyer can close without waiting for bank underwriting, which helps when a house has deferred repairs or when tenants are in place. You share the address, the condition and your goals, then review a written offer.

Closing takes place at a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder. If the property is a rental, sort out the lease, deposits and city license steps with the buyer before the closing date.

sections.h2: What do South Salt Lake sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Check these items before you accept any offer:

  • Whether every unit in a duplex or converted basement has a building permit on file.
  • Whether a rental license is current, and whether inspections were passed.
  • Any open code complaint about weeds, vehicles or trash.
  • Who lives in the house, and whether a lease or deposit must transfer.

A cash buyer that knows these answers up front can give a cleaner offer.

faqs.q: Which county is South Salt Lake in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The county Assessor values your house, the Treasurer collects the tax and the Recorder files your deed. Granite School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When is South Salt Lake property tax due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the late fee falls to 1% if you pay by January 31, per the Salt Lake County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my South Salt Lake house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a rental license with on-site building and fire inspections first, and operating without one is a Class C misdemeanor. Good Landlord certification reduces the fee.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: Only under the city's pending STR ordinance, which limits STRs to owner-occupied or primary-resident properties and bars them in ADUs. The ordinance was issued October 15, 2026, so check the city page for the final code.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in South Salt Lake?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the median value of owner-occupied homes at $410,200 for 2020 to 2024. That is a survey median, so your house may differ based on condition, lot and location.
